surfaces.part: central large red cap with white spot

answer.evidence: Three toadstools. The central cap (rows 4-7) is a dome whose width goes 4, 7, 7, 5 and has a white spot on its upper surface (row 6 at x=8). A dark underside row at row 7 sits under that cap's light top. The left and right caps (rows 8-11) both reach width 11 at rows 9-10 and narrow to 7 at row 11. Each cap is a rounded top with a dark underside, so each reads as a top surface and not a flat front strip. The grey stems below (rows 11-13, width 4 then 2) give a short front/support face. The overall impression is a 3/4 view of caps seen from above with stems visible, though the front face is small and organic.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny prop, under one tile, so the per-tile tone count of 0 says nothing and I judged by eye. It has 16 distinct colours across a few caps and stems, which is rich for something this small. Each red cap seems to step through highlight, light, mid and dark red, with white spots and cream stems. That is about 4 steps, a little under the trees' 5-6, which is expected at this size. Only 18% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans dark red-brown beside the caps rather than being a black sticker line. There are no flat 5x5 fills (0% near-flat coverage). It reads as less dense than the full trees, but a careful artist would accept it as a grass-decor prop beside them without it looking flat. The board is very small, so some of this is hard to verify, and the verdict is a marginal pass.
